bugs.name: Unmatched release search shows no empty-state feedback
bugs.summary: After searching for “no-such-release-query-zzq-2026,” the release list disappears and the screen shows no no-results or empty-state message.
bugs.expected: When a release search has no matches, the list area should clearly indicate that no releases matched the query.
bugs.actual: After searching for “no-such-release-query-zzq-2026,” the release list disappears and the screen shows no no-results or empty-state message.
reproSteps: Open the field-notes repository Releases list.
Enter “no-such-release-query-zzq-2026” in Search and submit it.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the absence of a no-results message as a product bug. An empty release list for a query with no matches is not sufficient evidence of a defect.

bugs.name: Release edit form does not let users change the tag
bugs.summary: The saved draft release editor displays its existing tag as read-only while title and notes remain editable.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation was that a saved draft release tag could be changed directly in the web editor.
bugs.actual: The web editor keeps tag and target read-only. Title and notes save while remaining a draft. Deleting and recreating an owned draft with a corrected tag worked without publishing.
reproSteps: Create and save a tagged draft release in a disposable repository.
Observe that the existing tag is static text while title and notes are editable.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the claim: direct tag editing is not an established supported web-editor capability. The pinned web route, form and handler deliberately edit a release under its existing tag. Fresh GUI validation confirmed the displayed restriction and a working delete/recreate correction path. A new-tag draft does not create a Git ref and the separate API supports tag changes; those facts do not establish a promised GUI operation. This rejection does not assess attachment loss during delete/recreate as a separate defect.
